reading.body:
Robert Latta's AI record is seven committee contributions from AI companies and five recorded votes, with one sponsored AI security bill. The money runs from June 2025 to June 2026 and totals $13,500 across Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Qualcomm PACs.

The contributions are the densest part of the record. Google gave twice in June 2025, $2,500 and $1,000 eight days apart. Amazon gave twice, $2,500 in September 2025 and $2,500 in June 2026. Microsoft, Meta, and Qualcomm each appear once. The dates are filing dates, so they mark when money was reported, not when any vote was cast.

The legislative side is thinner and mostly not AI-specific. Only H.R. 9914, the Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act, and H.R. 6875, the AI OVERWATCH Act, are named as AI measures. The other votes, on H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, and S. 146, are recorded as AI bills by this site's classification but the data does not say what they contain.

What this does not show is causation or intent. Contributions and votes sit on one timeline because they share a date order, not because one produced the other. The record also covers only what this site tracks, so it is a partial view of a member's fundraising and floor activity, not a complete one.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Robert Latta: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
